page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 3.2 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is a key highlight, with 2500 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity bundled directly with the instance. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with the Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0 and Geekbench text processing score of 2791.0 both ranking in the top tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core capabilities are more limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth read-only tests also register in the lower tier, though write bandwidth and database operations maintain average performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.xlarge offers high storage and memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it a specialized choice for workloads requiring large local datasets without needing massive multi-core processing. The hardware configuration is well-suited for database operations, local caching, text processing, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks. It is less optimal for highly parallelized compute-intensive tasks or software compilation due to its lower multi-core scaling.
